note: Faithful rendering of Avalokitavrata's exposition of the inference and the Vaiśeṣika alternative; the root verse is slightly loosened ('Since these aggregates exist') but the argument and its members are correctly reproduced.

errors.why: The Tibetan says nirvāṇa (mya ngan las 'das pa) is accomplished from it; rendering it 'liberation' blurs it with rnam par thar pa, which the next sentence introduces as a separate synonym.

note: Sound translation of the tantric commentary; lemmata and glosses are correctly separated and the subjugation section is accurate.

errors.why: ltung byed is pātayantika (Pali pācittiya); 'pāpayattika' is not a Vinaya term.

errors.english: a fully ordained member of this legal tradition [note: meaning a fellow monk of the same monastic community]
errors.why: chos 'di pa means one belonging to this Dharma (a Buddhist, as opposed to an outsider), not a 'legal tradition' or the same local community.
rgya shug is juniper; the item is a juniper berry/seed.

note: Accurate on the structure of the striking offence (body / thrown / connected, minimal limits, moment of contact); a few lexical slips.

errors.why: nga smra'o is the Buddha's first-person 'I declare'.

note: Generally faithful rendering of the sūtra quotations on heavy misdeeds and bodhicitta purifying downfalls; one speaker reversal and some unmarked inline glosses.

errors.english: This is found in many (sutras) discourses endowed with the (paramitas) perfections and should be viewed in the systems of (mantra) secret formula; tantra as well.
errors.why: The Tibetan is an open clause ('[the author,] having looked at the many pāramitā sūtras and the mantra systems, and ...') leading into the next side, not a statement that the quotation is found in those sūtras.

note: The three 'how is the proponent of emptiness to be understood' sections are rendered accurately; only the closing transition is misconstrued.

errors.why: sdud par byed pa'i tshig is 'the words of the compiler' (saṃgītikāra), the standard label for the narrative frame of a tantra.

fix.replace: are the words of the compiler

errors.english: The Body, Speech, and Mind Vajra of those, which causes everyone to tremble, is the nature of the Wrathful Mantra; it is manifested from this very Body and so forth.
errors.why: The wrathful one who terrifies the body-speech-mind vajra of all the Tathāgatas, embodying the mantra, was drawn forth from the Lord's own body etc.; the preceding 'he is the one of all the Tathagatas' is garbled.

note: The samaya of excrement and urine and the pratyāhāra reading are correct, but the Vajrakrodha passage is confused and the compiler's frame is mislabelled.

errors.english: You are indeed all the Buddhas, and I am all the Bodhisattvas themselves.
errors.why: The verse says 'I myself am all the Buddhas, all the Bodhisattvas'; there is no 'you', and the point is self-identification, hence 'worship your own self'.

fix.find: You are indeed all the Buddhas, and I am all the Bodhisattvas themselves.
fix.replace: I am indeed all the Buddhas and all the Bodhisattvas themselves.

errors.english: Through the profound devotion of the Great Holder [note: Vajradhara]
errors.why: lhag par mos pa is the yogin's adhimokṣa (resolve/visualisation) of being Great Vajradhara, not Vajradhara's own devotion.

errors.english: a single portion of the supreme activity at the conclusion of the Supreme Victorious Mandala
errors.why: These are the named samādhis maṇḍalarājāgrī and karmarājāgrī ('supreme king of maṇḍalas', 'supreme king of action'), not a 'victorious mandala' and 'supreme activity'.

errors.english: [note: referring to the stabilization of vital essences]
errors.why: khu ba phyung means the fluid is drawn out/emitted from the samaya, not stabilised.

note: Readable, but the key verse inverts the self-identification, the yogin's adhimokṣa is reassigned to Vajradhara, and the samādhi names are not recognised.

errors.why: Slob dpon Yang dag bden pa is Wŏnch'ŭk's name for Paramārtha (Zhendi), whose own construction the explanation is said to be; 'Satyavadin/True Speaker' is a mistranslated proper name (also in 'Master Satyavadin's commentary').

fix.replace: the master Paramārtha (Yang dag bden pa)

errors.english: Because the nature of that phenomenon consists of both the cognition of distinction and the nature of distinction, they are one.
errors.why: The verse gives two reasons against the universal (difference is cognised, and the property would be one with things of distinct nature); the English turns the reductio into a positive conclusion 'they are one'.

note: The apoha argument against a universal both distinct and non-distinct is mostly followed, but the opening is mistranslated and the root verse's reasoning is garbled.
